# ap - Agent Instructions

`ap` (short for **autoproject**) is an opinionated automation tool for gke-labs projects. It uses a "convention over configuration" approach to handle common development tasks.

## Repository Root and Subtrees

- The git repository root (containing `.git`) is the only root; configuration is read from `<repo>/.ap/`.
- Commands operate on a subtree of the repository: either the positional target when specified (e.g., `ap e2e autodeploy`, `ap deploy <dir>`), the subtree of the current working directory, or the whole repository when run from the root.
- Subtree overrides: A `.ap/` directory in a subtree can override configuration options for files beneath it. The effective configuration for a path is the base configuration with keys overridden by the nearest enclosing subtree `.ap/go.yaml`, walking up to the root (only present keys override, absent keys inherit, lists such as `skip` replace, explicitly written keys win, mapping sections merge per key). Overrides apply to `gofmt`, `govet`, `govulncheck`, `tidy`, `skip`, `lint` (analyzer modes and baselines under `lint.analyzers.<name>`, e.g. `lint.analyzers.droppedErrors.mode: error`), and `toolchain`, while tool version files (`protoc.yaml`, `docker.yaml`, `buildctl.yaml`, `helm.yaml`, `kind.yaml`, `kubectl.yaml`, `kustomize.yaml`) and `.ap/ap.yaml` remain root-only. Subtree `.ap/` directories do not change discovery, build context, image naming, or generated presubmits. Example subtree `.ap/go.yaml`:
  ```yaml
  govulncheck:
    enabled: false
  ```

## Initializing / Onboarding Projects

To onboard a repository or subdirectory onto `ap`, run `ap init`:

```bash
go run github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/ap@latest init --copyright-holder "<Organization>"
```

- Creates `.ap/` with starter `ap.yaml` (`version: latest`), `go.yaml`, and `headers.yaml`.
- Pass `--license none` to disable license header checks, or `--license apache-2.0` (default).
- Pass `--generate` to initialize and generate CI presubmits in one step:

```bash
go run github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/ap@latest init --copyright-holder "<Organization>" --generate
```

## Recommended Workflow for Agents

When making changes to an AP-managed project, coding agents should follow this verification sequence:

0.  **Initialize (if onboarding)**: If the repository or component is not yet configured for `ap`, run `ap init`.
1.  **Generate Code**: Run `ap generate` to update any generated files, CI scripts, or manifests (note: `ap generate` also runs `ap fmt` to format code, tidy Go modules, and stamp license headers).
    -   Run `ap generate --verify` (or `ap verify-generate`) to verify that generated files are up to date: in-process generators are verified by proving perturbed outputs are restored, and container plugin generate tasks are verified by comparing staged outputs against the checkout without modifying the working tree.
    -   Action versions emitted into `.github/workflows/ci-presubmits.yaml` live in `ap/pkg/generate/action.yml` (pinned to commit SHAs with `# ratchet:` comments) and are updated by Dependabot across `/` and `/ap/pkg/generate` in a single group with no manual step expected; if a Dependabot pull request ever updates only one of the two files, the fix is `ap generate`.
2.  **Lint**: Run `ap lint` to ensure code follows project style and quality guidelines. Analyzer settings are configured under `lint.analyzers.<name>` (e.g. `lint.analyzers.droppedErrors.mode: error`).
    -   Runs go vet, govulncheck, tidy checks (`go mod tidy -diff`, configurable via `tidy.enabled` in `.ap/go.yaml`, failing with the diff if untidy), and custom analyzers.
    -   When adopting a strict check at `mode: error` with existing findings, run `ap lint --write-baseline`, commit the `.ap/*-baseline.txt` files, and fix entries over time.
    -   Task scripts must be portable across macOS and Linux; `ap lint` flags known GNU-only / bash-4-only constructs.
3.  **Test**:
    -   Run `ap test` for unit and integration tests (supports `--test.race` to run under the data race detector; repos can configure `test.race: true` in `.ap/ap.yaml` to enable it by default in `ap test` and generated CI presubmits).
    -   Run `ap e2e` for end-to-end tests.
        -   If a root has `tests/e2e` Go tests, `ap e2e` runs `RUN_E2E=1 go test -v -count=1 -timeout 30m ./tests/e2e/...`. A `dev/tasks/test-e2e*` script at the same root runs before them and is for setup only (build a binary, prepare a cluster, free disk space); it must not run the Go tests itself, or they run twice.
        -   If a kind worker's kubelet restarts in a loop while other nodes are Ready, check inotify limits; CI jobs that create more than one kind cluster should raise them with a visible `sudo sysctl -w` step.

## Deployment

-   **Command**: `ap deploy`
-   **Targets**: Positional arguments select targets: `ap deploy <dir>` applies every manifest under any `k8s/` directory beneath `<dir>`, `ap deploy <dir>/k8s/<file>.yaml` applies a single file and builds only images that file references, `ap deploy <dir>/kustomization.yaml` builds with `kustomize build` and applies the generated YAML as a manifest with ApplySet support (a kustomization target builds no container images for now), and Git URLs (e.g. GitHub web links, raw links, or Kustomize-style syntax with `?ref=`) clone locally to `~/.cache/ap/git` and deploy from the clone.
-   **Images**: `ap` automatically builds Docker images found in the `images/<image-name>` directory. Built images deployed with `:latest` are pinned by digest (`tag@sha256`) in applied manifests so redeploying always rolls pods to the new image.
-   **Kubernetes**: `ap` deploys Kubernetes manifests located in the `k8s` directory.
-   **Kind**: When the current context is a kind cluster, `ap deploy` works with no `IMAGE_PREFIX`, building locally, loading images into the kind cluster using a unique tag, and applying.
-   **Cluster**: Use `--cluster=kind://<name>` to target a specific kind cluster or `--cluster=<context>` to target a kubeconfig context.
-   **Namespace**: Passing `-n <namespace>` retargets namespaced objects to the target namespace while logging changes and applying cluster-scoped objects as-is.
-   **ApplySet**: Pass `--applyset=[RESOURCE[.GROUP]/]NAME` to track deployments with KEP-3659 ApplySet labels and maintain parent metadata.
-   **BuildKit**: Configure remote BuildKit using `--buildkit-host` or `BUILDKIT_HOST` (e.g. `k8s://namespace/service`); the `k8s` shorthand expands to `k8s://autodeploy-system/buildkit`. Reaching an in-cluster BuildKit uses a private unix socket and opens no local port.
-   **Buildctl**: The buildkit path uses the pinned `buildctl`.
-   **Registry Prefix**: `IMAGE_PREFIX` defaults to `images.local`, assuming an in-cluster image registry and its node agent.
-   **Skip Push**: Use `--skip-push` to skip pushing built images to the registry.
-   **Workload Readiness**: `ap deploy` waits in parallel for all applied Deployments, DaemonSets, and StatefulSets to be ready within a single timeout (`--timeout`, default `5m`). On failure, it reports unavailable replicas, pod waiting reasons, and last termination messages. Use `--wait=false` to skip waiting.
-   **ConfigMap/Secret Hash Suffixing**: Annotate a `ConfigMap` or `Secret` in plain manifests with `infra.labs.gke.io/hash-suffix: "true"` (any other value is an error) to append a deterministic 10-character SHA-256 content-hash suffix to its name and rewrite pod-spec references (`envFrom`, `env[].valueFrom`, `volumes[]` including `projected.sources[]` and volume `secretRef`, `imagePullSecrets`) in `Deployment`, `DaemonSet`, `StatefulSet`, `Job`, `CronJob`, and `Pod` manifests in the same namespace so config changes trigger a rollout. References from other kinds are not rewritten, so only annotate objects consumed by pods; unannotated objects and kustomization targets are left untouched. Each suffixed object is labeled `infra.labs.gke.io/hash-suffix-of: <original name>`, and after a successful apply and `--wait`, `ap deploy` removes superseded objects carrying that label in the namespace (skipped on wait failure, `--wait=false`, or `--dry-run`).
-   **Manifest Scope**: Manifests are applied as written apart from image references, namespace retargeting, and opt-in content-hash suffixes; `ap deploy` does not install missing CRDs or create Secrets.

## Tool Management

- `ap tool install [dir]` creates symlinks for managed tools (`buildctl`, `helm`, `kind`, `kubectl`, `kustomize`, `docker`, `docker-buildx`, `protoc`, `go`) pointing to `ap` for busybox-style dispatch to pinned tool binaries. In a repository, it defaults to `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin`. Discovered task scripts have `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin` prepended to `PATH` automatically. Scripts should call tools by name and never download them; `ap` provides them on `PATH`.
- `ap bash <script> [args...]` runs a bash script from the repository root with `${REPO_ROOT}/.build/bin` on `PATH` and `REPO_ROOT` exported (`#!/usr/bin/env -S ap bash`, requires coreutils 8.30+).
    -   Scripts should assume bash 4+, and `ap bash` warns when the local bash is older.

## Kubernetes Manifests

When writing Kubernetes manifests, follow these guidelines:

-   **Do not specify `imagePullPolicy`**: Kubernetes will automatically set a reasonable default (e.g., `Always` if the tag is `:latest`, `IfNotPresent` otherwise).
-   **Image Naming**: The image name should map to the directory name under `images`. For example, a Dockerfile at `images/foo/Dockerfile` will result in an image named `${IMAGE_PREFIX}/foo`. In your manifest, you should specify the image as `foo` or `foo:latest`. `ap` will handle the prefixing during deployment.

## Plugin Configuration

Plugins are declared in `.ap/plugins.yaml`. A plugin specifies an immutable digest-pinned image (`image: <repo>@sha256:...`) or a Dockerfile (`dockerfile: <path>` relative to the declaring repository, or a Git URL such as `dockerfile: https://github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/blob/<commit>/ap/images/ap-plugin-astro/Dockerfile`) built automatically before discovery using the source repository root as context (following the same builder settings as other images, such as `BUILDKIT_HOST` and `--buildkit-host`), with optional `network: false` (default) and `enabled: false` (for subtree overrides). Pinned commit URLs resolve offline without contacting the remote once the image is built, while moving references (branches or tags) contact the remote on discovery. Plugins declare their activation file patterns as repository-relative paths (e.g. `**/astro.config.*`, `docs/astro.config.*`; a bare name matches only at the top level), which `ap ls` discovers per directory across the repository. Plugins communicate with `ap` via gRPC over stdio (`ap.plugin/v1alpha1`), streaming repository view files and receiving logs and output chunks placed through `fileutils.UntrustedRoot` (no volume mounts; files travel over the stream).

`image:` plugins run through the `clix` sandbox library (`github.com/gke-labs/clix/sandbox`), using the first usable sandbox backend (`FirstUsable`: `docker`, `apple-container`, `chroot`, `proot`). `ap` does not read `CLIX_SANDBOX`, and there is no flag or config setting; if no backend works, `ap` lists what was tried and why each failed. Plugins default to no network (`network: none`). `dockerfile:` plugins continue to require Docker (they are built into the local Docker engine and referenced by image ID); on a host without Docker, a `dockerfile:` plugin fails with an error naming the plugin and stating Docker is required, while `image:` plugins work.

The Astro container plugin (`ap/images/ap-plugin-astro/Dockerfile`, or declared via Git URL `https://github.com/gke-labs/gke-labs-infra/blob/<commit>/ap/images/ap-plugin-astro/Dockerfile`) activates on `**/astro.config.*` to build static documentation sites into `dist/` offline (`--network none`) during `ap build` with no Node.js on the host. When declared via a Git URL, `ap` clones the repository at the resolved commit into `AP_CACHE_DIR` and builds using that repository's root as context, providing `go.mod`, `ap/`, and npm dependencies (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`) in the build context. A repository supplies or pins npm dependencies via `package.json` and `package-lock.json` alongside the Dockerfile, installed hermetically at image build time with `npm ci`.

## Task Output

Every leaf task runs with buffered output, printing a status line per task (`=== <name> (ok|FAILED, <duration>)`) and emitting captured output only on failure (pass `-v=1` to print output for passing tasks); passing tasks print only warning-level log lines (`log.Warn(...)`). `ap e2e` prints leaf task output at default verbosity so test execution results are visible in CI job logs. When `$ARTIFACTS` is set, every leaf task writes its buffered output under `$ARTIFACTS/tasks/` (subdivided by task tree parent names, e.g. `$ARTIFACTS/tasks/lint-repo/go-lints/go-lint-autodeploy/go-vet.log`, with numeric suffixes on collisions) whether it passed or failed; task names are free-form human-readable strings, and the first line of each log file is the task's human-readable name. Tasks obtain a `scoped.Logger` via `scoped.Log(ctx)` that writes directly into this buffer using structured key/value pairs (`Error`, `Warn`, and `Info` are always shown at `-v=0`, `Debug` shows at `-v=1`, `Fine` at `-v=2`, `Finer` at `-v=3`, and `Finest` at `-v=4`; command-level lines use the same form). Built images log a summary line (`built image image=<image> builder=<builder> duration=<duration> sent=<bytes>`), where buildctl reports context bytes sent and Docker omits `sent` because buildx does not expose them.
